# zlartg

> Generates a plane rotation with real cosine and complex sine.

<section class="intro">

```text
[  C         S  ] . [ F ]  =  [ R ]
[ -conjg(S)  C  ]   [ G ]     [ 0 ]
```

where C is real and `C**2 + |S|**2 = 1`.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlartg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlartg';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlartg( f, g, c, s, r ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `Complex128Array` | First component (input only) |
| `g` | `Complex128Array` | Second component (input only) |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · On exit, the real cosine of the rotation |
| `s` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex sine of the rotation |
| `r` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex result |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The first component of vector to be rotated.
- `g`: The second component of vector to be rotated.
- `c`: The cosine of the rotation.
- `s`: The sine of the rotation.
- `r`: The nonzero component of the rotated vector.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlartg.strided( f, offsetF, g, offsetG, c, offsetC, s, offsetS, r, offsetR ) → void
```

Generates a plane rotation with real cosine and complex sine, using alternative indexing semantics.

```text
[  C         S  ] . [ F ]  =  [ R ]
[ -conjg(S)  C  ]   [ G ]     [ 0 ]
```

where C is real and `C**2 + |S|**2 = 1`.

F and G are unchanged on return.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `Complex128Array` | First component (input only) |
| ↳ `offsetF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `f` (in complex elements) |
| `g` | `Complex128Array` | Second component (input only) |
| ↳ `offsetG` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `g` (in complex elements) |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · On exit, the real cosine of the rotation |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `c` |
| `s` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex sine of the rotation |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `s` (in complex elements) |
| `r` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex result |
| ↳ `offsetR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `r` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The first component of vector to be rotated.
- `g`: The second component of vector to be rotated.
- `c`: The cosine of the rotation.
- `s`: The sine of the rotation.
- `r`: The nonzero component of the rotated vector.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlartg()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLARTG`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlartg.f90).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlartg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlartg';

// Generate a plane rotation such that [ c s; -conj(s) c ] * [ f; g ] = [ r; 0 ]:
const f = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 1.0 ] );
const g = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, -2.0 ] );
const c = new Float64Array( 1 );
const s = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const r = new Complex128Array( 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
zlartg( f, g, c, s, r );
console.log( c[ 0 ], reinterpret( s, 0 ), reinterpret( r, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
zlartg.strided( f, 0, g, 0, c, 0, s, 0, r, 0 );
console.log( c[ 0 ], reinterpret( s, 0 ), reinterpret( r, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLARTG`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLARTG generates a plane rotation so that

$$
\begin{bmatrix} C & S \\ -\overline{S} & C \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} F \\ G \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} R \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
$$

where C is real and $C^2$ + \|S\|\*\*$2 = 1$.

The mathematical formulas used for C and S are

```text
sgn(x) = {  x / |x|,   x != 0
```

```text
{  1,         x  = 0
```

$$
R = \operatorname{sgn}(F) \, \sqrt{|F|^2 + |G|^2}
$$

$$
C = |F| / \sqrt{|F|^2 + |G|^2}
$$

$$
S = \operatorname{sgn}(F) \, \overline{G} / \sqrt{|F|^2 + |G|^2}
$$

Special conditions:

-   If $G=0$, then $C=1$ and $S=0$.
-   If $F=0$, then $C=0$ and S is chosen so that R is real.

When F and G are real, the formulas simplify to $C = F/R$ and $S = G/R$, and the returned values of C, S, and R should be identical to those returned by DLARTG.

The algorithm used to compute these quantities incorporates scaling to avoid overflow or underflow in computing the square root of the sum of squares.

This is the same routine ZROTG fom BLAS1, except that F and G are unchanged on return.

Below, wp=\>dp stands for double precision from LA\_CONSTANTS module.

### Further Details

Based on the algorithm from

Anderson E. (2017) Algorithm 978: Safe Scaling in the Level 1 BLAS ACM Trans Math Softw 44:1--28 https://doi.org/10.1145/3061665

</section>
